To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hadronic neutron and proton masses can be reproduced by chiral soliton quantization of the nucleon in both the linear σ-model and the chiral chromo-dielectric model.

the neutron-proton mass splitting is a consequence of an isospin breaking term, and that it can be reproduced in chiral soliton approaches to the nucleon if the collective quantization method is not applied.

the hadronic mass splitting between the neutron and proton in the chiral soliton model of valence quark with and without confinement can be obtained from an up- and a down-quark mass splitting of 3.2 and 3.0 MeV, respectively, and that the chiral collective quantization of the chiral chromodielctric and linear sigma-models, in contrast to the angular-momentum collective quantization, does not yield the hadronic mass splittings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: 1.
the description of the nucleon as an excitation of the chiral field.
the study of the hadronic neutron proton mass splitting within a chiral solitonic description of the nucleons as well as the study of the chiral symmetry breaking in the hadronic sector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the collective quantization method is unable to describe the neutron-proton mass splitting in chiral soliton model of valence quark.
, in the framework of the models considered, a quark mass difference is the only source of the hadronic mass splitting between the neutron and proton.
the hadronic splitting is not a direct consequence of a quark mass splitting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hadronic splitting is a consequence of the quark mass splitting in chiral models of valence and current quarks with and/or without confinement.
the chiral soliton model is a very useful tool to investigate properties of hadrons, in particular of the nucleon.

the chiral chromo-dielectric model and the chiral sigma-model are able to describe the nucleon as chiral soliton and the hadronic mass differences between nucleons and hyperons in terms of the quark masses and the confinement potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the hadronic neutronproton mass splitting can be understood in terms of an isospin symmetry breaking term in the Lagrangian, provided the collective quantization method is replaced by an angular-momentum projection technique.

the chiral chromo-dielectric model and the sigma-model are able to reproduce the experimental value of the neutron-proton hadronic mass splitting for a choice of the quark masses which is compatible with the experimental values.
the collective quantization method does not provide the correct value for the hadron mass splitting.
